Trace String: Healing: By touch, identifies the location and general severity of one injury: for example, a surface cut versus deeper damage. Blood: A bead of blood marks one visible creature until the end of her next turn. Hycinthia can follow its movement within 30 ft, even through smoke or a crowd, but not through a solid wall.

Healing: Locates a hidden bleed or identifies which of several visible wounds is most urgent. Blood: A thin blood line follows a marked creature for 3 rounds within 30 ft. Hycinthia ignores ordinary visual concealment when aiming her next Blood String at it.

Healing: Distinguishes physical trauma from signs of poison, infection, or illness in one patient. It identifies the kind of problem, not automatically its exact cause. Blood: Marks two creatures for 1 minute. While within 60 ft, she knows their direction and can tell which one is visibly injured.

Healing: Examines up to three touched patients in succession and learns who will deteriorate first without immediate care. Blood: Blood markers anticipate a marked creature’s movement. Her next Blood String against one marked target deals +1d6 damage and ignores ordinary visual concealment. The marker then ends.

Healing: Maps complex, interacting injuries in one living patient, identifying what must be treated first and what an attempted repair might worsen. Blood: Maintains up to four blood markers for 1 minute. She can direct a Blood String at a marked target she can reach around ordinary visual obstruction, but still cannot cast through a solid barrier or beyond the String’s range.
Seam String: Healing: Closes a minor cut and restores 1d8 VP to a touched creature injured by torn soft tissue. i Blood: Sends a fine filament up to 15 ft for 1d6 slashing damage.

Healing: Closes a deeper cut, stops its ordinary bleeding, and restores 2d8 VP. It does not remove infection or repair a broken bone. Blood: Deals 2d6 slashing damage. On a failed POT save, the filament also catches a hand or weapon, preventing that hand from being used until the end of the target’s next turn.

Healing: Repairs a significant tear in muscle or skin and restores 3d8 VP. The patient may still need rest before using the injured area normally. Blood: Deals 3d6 slashing damage. On a failed POT save, Hycinthia may pull a held object free or pin one limb until the start of her next turn.

Healing: Joins extensive fresh soft-tissue damage and restores 4d8 VP. It cannot replace tissue that is missing. Blood: Deals 4d6 slashing damage and, on a failed POT save, Restrains one target for 1 round. The binding can be cut or broken normally.

Healing: Over 10 minutes, rejoins freshly separated tissue when the original tissue is present and viable; restores 5d8 VP. It cannot grow a replacement limb. Blood: Splits into several cutting seams. Divide 6d6 slashing damage among up to three targets within 30 ft; one target that fails a POT save is Restrained for 1 round.
Set String: Healing: Supports a sprain or unstable joint for 1 hour, allowing careful movement without worsening it. This is support, not a completed repair. Blood: Hardens blood around her forearm. She reduces the next physical hit by 1d6 damage, or makes one short strike for 1d6 bludgeoning damage.

Healing: Aligns a straightforward fracture and restores 1d8 VP. The bone remains fragile and needs ordinary recovery time. Blood: Forms a sturdier guard for 1 round, reducing one hit by 2d6, or a hardened strike dealing 2d6 bludgeoning damage.

Healing: Sets a complex break and stabilizes nearby damaged tissue; restores 2d8 VP. The patient cannot immediately use the limb at full strength. Blood: A hardened blood limb strikes for 3d6 bludgeoning damage. A target that fails a POT save is knocked Prone.

Healing: Over 10 minutes, repairs a badly fractured bone well enough for cautious use and restores 3d8 VP. Severe surrounding injuries still need other Strings. Blood: Maintains a blood brace for 3 rounds while concentrating. It reduces the first physical hit against her each round by 2d6, and she can make one 3d6 bludgeoning strike during that time.

Healing: Over 1 hour, rebuilds a shattered but still-present bone and restores 4d8 VP. Recovery afterward is still necessary. Blood: Raises a rigid 10-ft barricade for 3 rounds, or collapses that structure into one 5d8 bludgeoning strike. She cannot keep the barricade after using it to strike.
Ease String: Healing: Dulls pain from one touched injury until the end of the patient’s next turn. The patient can still tell that they are hurt. Blood: A blood wrap absorbs 1d6 damage from the next blow against Hycinthia before her next turn.

Healing: Reduces pain and muscle spasm for 1 minute, allowing examination or simple treatment without the patient fighting the pain. Blood: Wraps one target’s limb for 1d6 bludgeoning damage. On a failed POT save, its speed is reduced by 10 ft for 1 round.

Healing: Keeps a conscious patient steady through a painful procedure or injury for 10 minutes. It suppresses a penalty caused specifically by pain, not one caused by damaged anatomy. Blood: Deals 2d6 bludgeoning damage through a tightening strand. On a failed POT save, the target cannot take reactions until its next turn.

Healing: Eases pain and physical shock in up to three touched patients for 3 rounds. They can communicate and follow treatment instructions despite their injuries. t Blood: Sends wraps around up to three targets within 30 ft. Divide 4d6 bludgeoning damage among them; targets that fail a POT save have their speed halved for 1 round.

Healing: Keeps one injured, living patient functional through extreme pain for 1 minute. It does not restore VP, and any untreated injury remains when the effect ends. Blood: Concentrates crushing pressure on one target for 4d8 bludgeoning damage. On a failed POT save, it is Restrained until the end of its next turn.
Pulse String: Healing: Helps a touched, living patient maintain a steady breath for 1 minute while the cause of their difficulty is addressed. Blood: A short blood pulse deals 1d6 bludgeoning damage and pushes a target 5 ft on a failed RES save.

Healing: Steadies a dangerously racing or weak pulse for 3 rounds. It cannot overcome an untreated fatal wound on its own. t Blood: A stronger pulse deals 2d6 bludgeoning damage and pushes a target 10 ft on a failed RES save.

Healing: Sustains a living patient’s breathing and circulation for 3 rounds, buying time for Holdfast, Seam, or ordinary treatment. Blood: Sends a pulse down a 15-ft line for 3d6 bludgeoning damage to creatures in it. Those that fail a RES save are knocked Prone.

Healing: Restores breathing to a living patient who has just stopped and maintains it for 1 minute, provided the underlying injury can be treated. t Blood: A broad pulse in a 15-ft cone deals 4d6 bludgeoning damage and pushes creatures 15 ft on a failed RES save.

Healing: While Hycinthia remains in contact and concentrates, sustains the vital functions of one critically injured living patient for up to 1 minute. It is emergency support, not resurrection. Blood: Releases a focused, 30-ft blood surge for 6d8 bludgeoning damage to one target, pushing it up to 20 ft on a failed RES save.
Cleanse String: Healing: Clears a mundane irritant from a fresh wound and makes it safer to treat. It does not cure an established disease. Blood: Forms a fine blood needle that deals 1d6 piercing damage. It has no poisonous effect without a real toxin.

Healing: Suppresses the effects of one poison in a touched patient for 1 minute, buying time for treatment but not removing it. Blood: A needle deals 1d6 piercing damage. If she has contained an extracted toxin, a target failing a RES save is also Poisoned for 1 round.

Healing: Removes one ordinary poison or treats a straightforward infection in a living patient. Recovery from damage already done still takes time. Blood: Fires a contained blood needle for 2d6 piercing damage. With an actual extracted toxin, add 1d6 poison damage; the toxin is then spent.

Healing: Over 10 minutes, treats a severe infection or complicated poison, provided she can identify what she is drawing out. Blood: A blood spray in a 15-ft cone deals 3d6 piercing damage. If carrying an actual extracted toxin, creatures failing a RES save are Poisoned for 2 rounds; the toxin is spent.

Healing: Over 1 hour, purges a deadly toxin or serious disease from one living patient. It does not restore tissue the condition has already destroyed. Blood: A directed blood strike deals 5d6 piercing damage. If she has contained a potent, real toxin, one target also suffers that toxin’s agreed effect on a failed RES save; the toxin is spent.
Renewal String: Healing: Helps a resting, touched patient recover from ordinary exertion. Their next period of rest is more effective, but the String does not replace rest. Blood: Moves a blood strand with sudden speed. Hycinthia gains +10 ft movement this turn and makes one 1d6 slashing strike.
Healing: Over 1 minute of care, restores 1d8 VP to a living patient recovering from recent injury. Blood: Gains +10 ft movement this turn; one blood strike deals 2d6 slashing damage.

Healing: Over 10 minutes, restores 2d8 VP and eases ordinary physical fatigue. It does not remove magical Burnout. Blood: Sweeps blood through two quick arcs. Divide 3d6 slashing damage between up to two targets within 15 ft.

Healing: Over 10 minutes, restores 3d8 VP and allows the patient to recover from substantial exertion without worsening their injuries. Blood: Hycinthia moves up to 20 ft as her blood lashes along her path. Divide 4d8 slashing damage among up to three targets she passes.

Healing: Over 1 hour, restores 5d8 VP and supports recovery from severe but nonmagical exhaustion. It cannot erase Burnout or replace prolonged convalescence. Blood: Her blood becomes a brief, fast-moving storm. Divide 6d8 slashing damage among up to three targets within 30 ft. Afterward, she suffers Shaking Hands until her next Mend.
Cradle String: Healing: A golden lattice supports an injured, touched ally until Hycinthia’s next turn, reducing the next damage they take by 1d6. Blood: Interposes a small blood screen, reducing one incoming hit against herself or an adjacent ally by 1d6.

Healing: Holds one patient steady during movement for 1 minute, preventing that movement from aggravating an ordinary wound. Blood: A blood screen reduces one hit by 2d6 and can be positioned between an ally within 10 ft and an attacker.
Healing: Supports two touched injured allies for 3 rounds. Each has the next hit against them reduced by 2d6. Blood: Forms a 10-ft wall that provides cover until the start of Hycinthia’s next turn.

Healing: Wraps one living patient in a lattice for 3 rounds. It has a shared pool of 3d8 damage reduction and keeps their injuries from worsening during transport. Blood: A jagged 15-ft wall lasts 3 rounds while she concentrates. A creature forcing through takes 3d6 slashing damage once per round.

Healing: Shelters up to three allies within reach for 1 minute with a shared 5d8 damage-reduction pool. Hycinthia chooses which protected hit spends from the pool. Blood: Raises a 20-ft defensive dome for 3 rounds. It provides cover; once each round, a creature striking or crossing it takes 4d8 slashing damage.
Burden String: Healing: A touched ally regains up to 2 VP; Hycinthia loses the same amount. She can sense their pain clearly for a moment afterward. Blood: Shapes exposed blood into a reflexive 1d6 slashing counterstrike against a creature within 10 ft.

Healing: Transfers up to 4 VP of an ally’s recent injury to herself. It restores VP but does not remove a condition such as poison or a broken bone. Blood: A blood ribbon intercepts a blow against an ally within 10 ft, reducing it by 1d6, then strikes the attacker for 2d6 slashing damage.

Healing: Transfers up to 6 VP of injury from a willing ally within 10 ft. Hycinthia experiences the strain immediately. Blood: A blood lash reaches 30 ft and deals 3d6 slashing damage. If she has taken damage protecting an ally since her last turn, it deals +1d6.

Healing: Transfers up to 10 VP from a willing ally within 15 ft. She cannot pass that loss on again through Burden. Blood: Interposes blood between an ally and an attack, reducing damage by 2d6, then releases a 4d8 slashing counterstrike.

Healing: Transfers up to 15 VP from one willing ally, potentially keeping them in the fight at great risk to herself. It cannot take on an injury she could not survive. f Blood: Protects one ally within 20 ft from a hit, reducing damage by 3d8, and sends the blood outward for 6d8 slashing damage against one attacker.
Reweave String: Healing: Over 10 minutes, guides a fresh wound toward cleaner healing, reducing avoidable scarring. It does not restore VP immediately. Blood: Shapes a fine blood tool or hook that can manipulate a small object within 15 ft, or strike for 1d6 piercing damage.

Healing: Over 1 hour, repairs minor lingering muscle damage in a living patient and restores 1d8 VP. Blood: Forms an articulated hook dealing 2d6 piercing damage. On a failed POT save, it holds a hand or object in place until Hycinthia’s next turn.

Healing: Over 1 hour, reconnects a recently damaged tendon or nerve when the living tissue remains available; restores 2d8 VP. Full function may return gradually. Blood: Several precise blood filaments deal 3d6 piercing damage. On a failed POT save, they disarm the target or bind one limb for 1 round.

Healing: Over several hours of uninterrupted work, repairs serious damage to a living organ or complex tissue and restores 3d8 VP. Trace may be needed first to understand the injury. Blood: Creates a multi-part construct for 3 rounds while concentrating. It can guard one adjacent ally or strike a target within 30 ft for 4d8 piercing damage once during its duration.

Healing: Over days of treatment, reconstructs severe but survivable tissue damage, restoring 5d8 VP across the treatment. It requires living tissue and does not resurrect or automatically resolve supernatural wounds. f Blood: Weaves a complex blood construct for 1 minute while concentrating. Once per round it can guard an ally or make a 3d8 piercing strike; it is not alive or independently intelligent.
Loom String: Healing: Assesses two touched patients in quick succession and identifies which needs immediate help first. Blood: Splits blood into two short strands. Divide 1d6 slashing damage between up to two targets within 15 ft.

Healing: Divides 2d8 VP of healing between up to two touched allies in any amounts she chooses. Blood: Controls two strands within 30 ft. Divide 2d6 slashing damage between up to two targets, or use one strand to catch an object instead of dealing its share.

Healing: Divides 4d8 VP of healing among up to three allies within reach and stabilizes any of them who were at 0 VP before distributing the pool. Blood: Controls three strands for one cast. Divide 3d6 slashing damage among up to three targets; one target failing a POT save also loses its reaction until its next turn.

Healing: Divides 6d8 VP of healing among up to four touched allies. She may instead spend one die from the pool to stop one ally’s ordinary bleeding. Blood: Controls four strands within 30 ft. Divide 5d6 slashing damage among up to four targets; alternatively, sacrifice 2d6 from the pool to give an ally cover until her next turn.

Healing: Over 1 minute, divides 8d8 VP of healing among up to five living allies she can reach and touch. She may stabilize them first, but cannot restore anyone already dead. Blood: Weaves a battlefield network for 3 rounds while concentrating. It has a total 8d6 slashing-damage pool to spend across those rounds and can protect up to two allies with cover. Once the pool is spent, the network fades.
